**READ-ONLY. Modify no files. No commits, no staging, no npm install, no npm start (a dev server is already running on :3000 and belongs to the developer). Do not run `npm run lint` with appended args — `package.json` forwards `--`-args into a shell exec and `lint:fix` would rewrite files. Plain `npx tsc --noEmit` is fine and required.**

## Your spec
`.claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md` → "Agent C — TypeScript coverage". Read it. Your rubric is the repo's own rules:
- `.claude/rules/typescript.md` **in full** — no `any` without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible; no non-null assertion (`!`) without an inline comment; prefer `type` over `interface`; discriminated unions for variant/state modelling; utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes; `import type` for type-only imports; `satisfies` over `as`; `readonly` on props/arrays the receiver must not mutate; generic naming.
- `.claude/rules/components.md` → **Components** (props type name matches component name (`<Name>Props`), props-type placement rule — default at top of component file, move to `types.ts` only when consumed by sibling files or >~30 lines mixing with other shared types; required props non-optional and optional props use `?` with no `| undefined` unions; callback props named `onEventName`; JSDoc required on any component used by ≥2 callers and on any exported hook and on any utility with non-obvious behaviour).
- `.claude/rules/components.md` → **Hooks** (typed params, explicit return type, JSDoc with `@returns`) if any hook is in scope.
- `AGENTS.md` → **Type Definitions** section (component-specific prop types co-located at top of the component file; shared types in `overrides/app/types/`; **don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly**). That last clause matters a lot on this branch.

1. `cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa && npx tsc --noEmit` — run **once** for the whole branch. Report every error, and cross-reference which are in scope files vs pre-existing elsewhere. To establish the pre-existing baseline, you may also run it on a clean stash-free comparison only if you can do so **without modifying the working tree** — do NOT stash, do NOT check out another branch. Instead, judge pre-existing-ness by whether the erroring file is in the scope list.
2. `npm run lint` with **no appended arguments** — report the error/warning count and any entries pointing at scope files. Treat the total count as an invariant you must not change.

## Settled decisions — do NOT report these as defects
1. **`textStyle` lives in the recipe `.css.ts` files, not on JSX elements**, in all five `zimmProduct*` atoms. Deliberate. Do not flag.
2. `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` are **copy-first TypeScript ports of base SFCC `.jsx` files** per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule. Their structure, length, complexity, prop surface, upstream American spelling and raw px values are base-verbatim and must stay that way. **Do not flag base-inherited traits in these two files** — including base-shaped prop surfaces, base's own loose typing patterns where the port had to pick *something*, or missing JSDoc that base didn't have. DO flag anything Zimmermann *added*. Use `git diff origin/develop...HEAD -- <file>` plus the base originals at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` to tell added-from-base apart. **However**: a `.jsx`→`.tsx` port necessarily *invents* types where base had none, and those invented types ARE Zimmermann-authored — audit them. If the port used `any`, a `as` assertion, or a non-null `!` to get base JS to compile, that is in scope for you and must carry an inline reason per typescript.md.
3. `product-view/index.tsx` has one added optional `renderHeader` slot; its default export is intentionally a faithful SFCC bridge.
4. `formatPrice` is knowingly duplicated between the page/`productInfo.ts` and `staticProductHeader.tsx`, with reciprocal comments; settled, out of scope.

If a finding genuinely conflicts with one of these, say so explicitly and state the conflict rather than suppressing it.

## Weight your attention here
Per-commit reviews on this branch caught per-file invariants but missed **uniform** divergences — a pattern repeated identically across five files passed every individual review. So prioritise **type-level consistency across the new component set**:
- Do all five `zimmProduct*` atoms and both `zimmProduct*` molecules declare their props type the same way (name, `type` vs `interface`, placement, `readonly`, optionality, `import type` usage)? Where one differs, is the difference justified?
- Are the same product-shaped fields typed identically across them, or has each file hand-rolled a slightly different local shape for the same SFCC data? Check hard against AGENTS.md's "don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`/`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`" and typescript.md's "Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes" — a hand-copied product/price/variant shape repeated across seven files is exactly the uniform divergence I am looking for.
- `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`: what was added, and does it paper over a type that genuinely exists upstream (which would make the declaration both unnecessary and a silent `any` surface)?
- Any `any`, `as`, `!`, or implicit-`any` callback params in the Zimmermann-authored files, and whether each carries the required inline reason.

## Output
Return findings directly as your final message (do NOT write any .md report file). For each: absolute `file:line`, the exact rule breached **with the relevant sentence quoted** from the rule file (naming file + section), and a concrete fix. Group 🔴 must-fix / 🟡 should-fix / 🟢 nit. Report the raw `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` results verbatim-in-summary (counts + scope-relevant entries). State what passed and what you could not check.

---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

## 🔴 Must fix

**1. The `any` aliases re-declare types that provably exist upstream — AGENTS.md breach**
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:85-88` and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:102-104`

AGENTS.md → Type Definitions: *"don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly."*

Both files carry a near-verbatim comment block justifying `SfccProduct/Variant/Category/PriceData = any` on the grounds that *"`@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types."* That's true but **irrelevant** — `Product`/`Variant`/`Category` are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types, not retail-react-app ones. So typescript.md's *"No `any` without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible"* is met in letter but the stated reason is wrong, which is worse than no comment: it forecloses the fix.

I proved the types resolve under this exact project config (TS 5.9.3, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`), with three negative controls that all fired — wrong primitive type, non-existent namespace member, and omitted required `id`. `ShopperProductsTypes` is exported at `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts:69365` and carries `Product`, `Variant`, `Category`, `Image`, `VariationAttribute`, `VariationAttributeValue`.

Fix: `import type {ShopperProductsTypes} from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic'`, then alias to those. Should also clear 3 of the 15 lint warnings (product-view 708/791/904 — all `any`-in-template-literal caused by these aliases).

**2. `SfccVariationValue.image` is typed as a Product but the code reads `Image` fields**
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:91`, consumed at `:783` and `:791`

`image?: SfccProduct`, but line 791 reads `` `url(${image.disBaseLink || image.link})` ``. Upstream `Image` has `link: string` + `disBaseLink?: string`; upstream `Product` has **neither**. This only compiles because `SfccProduct = any`. Port-invented, so in scope per your carve-out. Fix: `image?: ShopperProductsTypes.Image`.

## 🟡 Should fix

**3. The hand-rolled variation shapes contradict upstream on required/optional**
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:91,94-99`

typescript.md: *"Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes... A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the original changes; a utility type doesn't."*

- `name: string` — upstream is `name?: string`. **Stricter than reality**, and it masks a latent crash: line 790 calls `name.toLowerCase()` unguarded.
- `value?: string` — upstream is `value: string` (required). **Gives up a guarantee.**
- `values: SfccVariationValue[]` (:98) — upstream `values?: Array<...>`. Stricter than reality.

`href` is legitimate — base genuinely decorates values with it (`use-variation-attributes.js:152`, `product-utils.js:232`). product-view:85, product-detail:102, `productInfo.ts:17`. AGENTS.md → Type Definitions puts Commerce Cloud entities in `overrides/app/types/` *"split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`"* — that directory holds only `contentful.ts` and `vendor.d.ts`. **This is the uniform divergence you asked me to hunt**: two files independently declare the same three aliases with a copy-pasted justification block.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:511`

typescript.md: *"Reach for `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the same as an `any` — comment why)."* Every *other* assertion in this file carries a "SDK param widening" rationale, so this one reads as an oversight rather than a decision. It's also unsound — the catch binding is `unknown` under `strict`, and a thrown non-Error has no `.message`. Fix: `showError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : undefined)` (`showError()` is already called argument-less elsewhere).

Recipe annotation style diverges three ways across the seven new recipes** — five use `} satisfies SystemStyleObject`; `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:25` uses a zero-arg function returning `Record<string, SystemStyleObject>` (looser than its own declared `parts`); `zimmProductMeta.css.ts:35` has no annotation and no `SystemStyleObject` import at all. **I checked whether this is a safety hole and it is not** — `satisfies SystemStyleObject` accepts both a typo'd property name (`flexDirectionn`) and a bogus nested value (`zIndex: {bogus: true}`), because `SystemStyleObject` carries a permissive string index signature.
